title: Gurnoor Brar's 4 for 30 sets up rain-hit DLS win as India go 2-0 up in New Zealand
dek: New Zealand were bowled out for 134 in Wellington; India were 113 for seven, four runs ahead of par, when rain ended play.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India beat New Zealand by four runs on the DLS method in a rain-hit second one-day international in Wellington on Saturday to take a 2-0 lead in the five-match series, after fast bowler Gurnoor Brar took a career-best four for 30.

New Zealand, put in to bat, were bowled out for 134 in 41 overs. India were 113 for seven after 26 overs, four runs ahead of the DLS par score of 109, when rain ended play.

## Brar and the seamers

Captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl in a match reduced to 47 overs a side after a rain delay, according to reports. India's seamers reduced New Zealand to 53 for five. Auqib Nabi removed Tim Seifert for a five-ball duck and Will Young for six, Anshul Kamboj had Henry Nicholls for 11, and Brar dismissed Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips with short balls.

Daryl Mitchell made 55 off 104 balls and added 59 for the sixth wicket with captain Mitchell Santner, who made 31, before Axar Patel had Mitchell caught off a mistimed drive. Brar had Santner caught behind by KL Rahul, and Kamboj bowled Blair Tickner to end the innings. Brar finished with four for 30 from 10 overs, Nabi two for 31, Axar two for 28 and Kamboj two wickets; reports differ on Kamboj's figures, giving two for 25 or two for 15. Arshdeep Singh went wicketless but conceded only 16 runs in seven overs.

"I just try to bowl that hard length, the lengths where batters try to pull," Brar said after the match, adding that the bounce and pace in New Zealand had helped him.

## A nervy chase

Chasing 135, India lost Gill for a first-ball duck and Virat Kohli for seven, both to Jacob Duffy, and Rohit Sharma for 23 to Kyle Jamieson. They slipped to 47 for four before Shreyas Iyer (30) and Rahul added 46 for the fifth wicket. Jamieson took three for 33 and Duffy three for 35, and India were seven wickets down when the rain returned, with Rahul unbeaten on 26. Brar was named player of the match, according to reports.

## Series so far

India won the first ODI in Auckland on Wednesday by five wickets, also in a rain-affected game, with Kohli making 74 and Arshdeep taking four wickets. The ODIs follow a five-match T20 series that India won 3-2.

## What happens next

The third ODI is in Hamilton on Tuesday, 10 November, starting at 7.30 am IST, according to reports. A win there would give India the series with two games to spare.
